question.text: SEBI places concentration limits on Category III AIFs. The fund may invest not more than what percentage of its Investable Funds or NAV in a single investee company (normal Cat III, not Large Value Fund)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the AIF Managers workbook (pp. 279-280), a Category III AIF shall not invest more than 10 percent of its Investable Funds or NAV in a single investee company. The relaxation for a Large Value Fund (LVF) under Category III raises this concentration limit to 20 percent of Investable Funds or NAV per investee. The Trap: 20 percent is the Large Value Fund relaxation, not the normal Category III limit. 25 percent is not a SEBI concentration figure for Category III. 5 percent is not the normal Category III single-investee limit either. Note: The 10 percent normal limit and the 20 percent LVF limit are both expressed as a percentage of Investable Funds or NAV in any single investee company, as stated on pp. 279-280 of the source.
